title: Germany – Ships and boats – Marine-Hafenschlepper und flexibler Fähigkeitsträger (Navy-Tug flex) - TNW
description: Für die Deutsche Marine sind über eine Rahmenvereinbarung bis zu 20 baugleiche Hafenschlepper mit Arbeitsdeck der Klasse 724, die den Vorgaben einer anerkannten Klassifikationsgesellschaft und der deutschen Flagge entsprechen, aus einer bereits laufenden Serienproduktion neu zu beschaffen. Dabei ist über den Einsatz als reinen Schlepper hinaus eine zusätzliche Verwendung als "flexibler Fähigkeitsträger" beabsichtigt, welcher die Aufnahme von zwei ISO 20-Fuß-Standardcontainern bzw. vier ISO 10-Fuß-Containern und eine technische Seeausdauer von mindestens sieben Tagen ermöglicht. Aufgrund der aktuellen sicherheitspolitischen Lage ist zum Zwecke der Eindämmung des laufenden hybriden Krieges Russlands gegen die Bundesrepublik Deutschland und ihre Verbündeten im Nord- und Ostseeraum eine kurzfristige Beschaffung (bis 2028) erforderlich. Ziel ist es, die bei der Deutschen Marine derzeit vorhandenen sechs ca. 35 Jahre alten, nicht mehr bedarfsdeckenden Hafenschlepper der Klasse 725 zu ersetzen. Die vorgenannten Hafenschlepper werden insbesondere für die Erfüllung nachfolgender Einsatzaufgaben beschafft: • Assistenz/Bugsieren/Manövrieren von Schiffen und Booten der Marine auf Reeden und im Hafen, • Schleppen von Marineschiffen, -booten und Geräten im Hafen und im küstennahen Seegebiet, • Begleiten von Seezielschießen inkl. Transport, Ausbringen und Schleppen von Seezielen, • Aufnahme von zwei ISO 20-Fuß- Standardcontainern bzw. vier ISO 10-Fuß-Containern, • Unterstützung bei Werfterprobungen, Standproben und Kompensationsfahrten, • Eisdienst in den Häfen, • Brandbekämpfung im Hafen und auf See, • Hilfeleistung bei Gewässerverunreinigung sowie • Sicherung und Bergung von Schiffen und Booten in See.

title: Germany – Contractor's all-risk insurance services – Projektversicherung DSD Starterpaket Scan-Med- München
description: Der gegenständliche Realisierungsabschnitt gehört zum DSD Starterpaket „Durchfahrbarkeit des Skandinavien–Mittelmeer Korridors“ (Scan-Med). Das gegenständliche Projekt der DB InfraGO AG als Bestandteil des DSD-Starterpakets umfasst die Ausrüstung des Korridors Scan-Med München mit DStW-Technik und ETCS Level 2 ohne Signale (L2oS), es teilt sich in 2 Abschnitte, Strecke 5510 München - Rosenheim und Strecke 5703 Rosenheim - Freilassing. Die Investitionssumme für dieses Projekt wird mit ca. EUR 600,0 Mio. veranschlagt. Hiervon sind bereits ca. EUR 13,5 Mio. über einen bestehenden Vertrag abgerechnet worden. Der hier neu ausgeschriebene Versicherungsvertrag wird den bestehenden Vertrag ablösen. Es wird mit einer derzeit geplanten Bauzeit bis zum 31.12.2031 gerechnet. Der Versicherungsvertrag beginnt nach Beendigung des Ausschreibungsverfahrens mit dem Datum des Zuschlages im Anschluss an eine derzeit bestehende Vorlaufdeckung. (Typ M) In der Haftpflichtversicherung beträgt die Deckungssumme je Schadenfall EUR 25.000.000 pauschal für Personen-, Sach- und Vermögensschäden, einschließlich der Leistungen aus der Umwelthaftpflichtversicherung. In der Planungshaftpflichtversicherung steht eine separate Deckungssumme je Schadenfall von EUR 10.000.000 pauschal für Sach- und Vermögensschäden zur Verfügung. Die vorgenannten Summen sind dreifach maximiert. Die Extendend Maintenance im Teil Bauleistungs- und Montageversicherung beträgt 42 Monate. Die Nachhaftung beträgt in der Haftpflichtversicherung 10 Jahre, in der Umwelthaftpflicht- und Umweltschadenversicherung 5 Jahre. Der generelle Selbstbehalt beträgt mindestens EUR 25.000. Für Personenschäden entfällt der Selbstbehalt. Im Falle einer erweiterten Planungsdeckung beträgt der Selbstbehalt EUR 100.000

title: Norway – Electrical supplies and accessories – Framework agreement electrical material
description: The Contracting Authority manages several churches, cemeteries and other properties, and therefore has an ongoing need for electrical supplies for operation and maintenance. The Contracting Authority intends to enter into a framework agreement with a single supplier. The purpose of the procurement is to ensure that the overall needs of Bergen kirkelige fellesråd for electrical supplies are met efficiently and appropriately. For larger projects, the Contracting Authority will ask the supplier for project prices, and transport and delivery will also be an important part of the contract. The Contracting Authority currently has a similar framework agreement with Onninen, which expires in January 2027. The new framework agreement is therefore expected to start in January 2027. The agreement will run for two (2) years from the date of signing. The Contracting Authority has an option to extend the agreement by one (1) year at a time, up to two (2) times. The maximum total term is four (4) years. An option is exercised by written notice from the Contracting Authority no later than three (3) months before the agreement expires. The agreement terminates automatically at the end of the agreement period. If all options are exercised, the expected total value of the procurement is NOK 10,000,000, with expected annual call-offs of NOK 2,500,000. The maximum contract value is NOK 15,000,000. These amounts are based on historical data.

description: Gebäudeplanung nach §§ 33 - 37 HOAI i.V.m. Anlage 10 HOAI, LPH 2 - 9.Die Gemeinde Randersacker beabsichtigt die Neukonzeption des Rathaus-Areals zum „Bürgerzentrum Randersacker“. Ziel ist es, unter Erhalt der denkmalgeschützten Rathausfassade den gestiegenen Raumbedarf der Verwaltung zu decken und zusätzlich Flächen für örtliche Vereine zu schaffen. Für die Umsetzung des erhöhten Flächenbedarfs steht der Bereich des leerstehenden Gebäudeteils "ehemals Beamtenwohnhaus" zur Verfügung. Das Gebäude soll aufgrund des Zustandes, der abweichenden Geschosshöhen, Raumzuschnitten und Brandschutzaspekten abgerissen werden. Die bestehenden Nutzungen (Weltkreisladen mit Touristen-Info, Festausschank, öffentliches WC) sind neu zu integrieren. Das gesamte Areal inklusive Vorplatz und Außenanlagen ist städtebaulich, gestalterisch, energetisch sowie durchgängig barrierefrei aufzuwerten.

title: Ballfield Maintenance
description: The United States Coast Guard Academy intends to solicit quotations for ballfield maintenance services at the Nitchman Field Complex in New London, Connecticut. The contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, materials, equipment, transportation, and incidentals necessary to maintain the Baseball, Softball, and track-and-field/practice soccer fields in accordance with NCAA specifications. Required services include seasonal late-winter/early-spring maintenance of the baseball and softball infields and turf areas, including scarifying, regrading, infield and warning-track material placement, lip removal, edging, rolling, turf repair, replacement and verification of home plates and pitching rubbers, baseline and mound adjustments, and bullpen and pitching-mound repairs. The contractor shall also perform June deep-tine hollow-core aeration and topdressing of all three fields. The anticipated contract consists of a one-year base period, January 1, 2027 through December 31, 2027, with four one-year option periods.

Progress Review Meeting(s): Any progress review meetings will be conducted by telephone or videoconference. Final Review Meeting: All communication will take place by telephone or videoconference. Problem Statement: Challenge Statement Summary The challenge is to provide the Department of National Defense (DND) and the Canadian Army (CA) a software solution to provide an airspace common operating picture so that it can plan, deconflict, and control uncrewed aircraft system (UAS) traffic, including their use of the radio frequency (RF) spectrum, in order to ensure the safe and efficient management of UAS to enable the Canadian soldier to successfully fight and survive on the future battlefield. Details: Essential Outcomes The proposed solution must: 1. Be Windows-based. 2. Allow a user to create and store flight plans, including radio frequency requirements. 3. Have a flight plan repository (database) that stores the 4D (3D + time) trajectories and spectrum requirements of all accepted flight plans. 4. Enable integration of supplemental data services such as crewed aircraft flight plans and weather. 5. Generate an optimal 4D flight path for UAS based on specific mission goals and physical limits. 6. Be able to check new flight requests against existing flight plans, airspace constraints (no-fly zones) and RF spectrum requests to detect conflicts and resolve them (via set priorities or a human decision). 7. Generate 4D blocks of deconflicted airspace (a "tunnel" or a "box") where a UAS is permitted to fly. Additional Outcomes The proposed solution should: 1. Analyze real-time data from UASs to prevent collisions and automatically adjust flight paths for UASs in controlled airspace. 2. Check in real-time whether a UAS is following its pre-approved, deconflicted trajectory. 3. Demonstrate capacity in having its critical components produced and sourced in countries within the NATO alliance, NATO Partners or Major Non-NATO Allies. To achieve this, Offerors are requested to provide as an attachment to their proposal, a list identifying the solution's critical components, the country of production and sourcing for each component. Critical components and requested information for each Critical components are defined below: Critical components: 1. Radio 2. Ground control station (GCS) 3. On-board computer 4. Any software Requested information: i. Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM): Name of the original equipment manufacturer of the product being sourced ii. OEM URL: Provide the URL of the OEM iii. Software: Confirm if developed by Offeror or outsourced iv. Product name: Provide the OEM's product name v. Model number: Provide the OEM's model and/or version number of the product vi. Product URL: Provide the URL of the OEM product, model, and version vii. Country of origin IMPORTANT NOTE: For this challenge, kindly disregard the Attachment requirements detailed at Section D in the Web-Portal, and instead adhere to the following: - The attachment measures 8.5" by 11" with a maximum size of 10Mb. - Only the following formats will be accepted: JPG, GIF, TIF, PDF or PNG. - The attachment must be clear and legible. Note: Including an attachment is not mandatory, but forms part of the Additional Outcomes, which is scored up to 10 points. The Applicant (Offeror) acknowledges that it is within Canada's sole discretion to determine whether the attachment is removed or included in the Offer. Background & Context The CA is undergoing a generational modernization effort to address the evolving nature of technology, the changing character of conflict, and the unravelling of the geopolitical system. The transformative changes being made are conceptually described in the CA publication Inflection Point 2025. This document provides the broad context for modernization and directs the development and acquisition of key systems; in particular, it states: Key to this transformation is the integration of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, robotics, autonomous and uncrewed systems. These capabilities will support a wide range of functions, from intelligence analysis and predictive modeling to targeting and operational execution. The CA, in recognizing this need, has purchased foreign robotics and autonomous systems of varying quality and has identified challenges purchasing systems that meet operational requirements, in particular related to cold-weather operations, and that have stable supply chains. Further, purchases have, in the past, been constrained by limited manufacturing capacity of industry partners. To address this, the Government of Canada's recently released policy Canada's Defence Industrial Strategy, emphasizes the need to develop a strong domestic industrial capacity to produce defence materiel. This policy directs the CA to seek solutions to operational problems through Canadian industry, which will both improve the CA's capability while providing the foundation of a strong defence industrial base able to scale production of quality defence material. To date, engagements with Canadian industry have revealed a wide variety of small/medium companies that have commercial technologies that could, with support, be tailored to military requirements.

title: Perusterveydenhuollon hoidon jatkuvuuden ammatinharjoittajamallin hankinta
description: Perusterveydenhuollon hoidon jatkuvuuden ammatinharjoittajamallin hankinta Hankinnan kohteena on yleislääkäripalveluiden hankinta ammatinharjoittajamallilla toteutettuna Pirkanmaan hyvinvointialueelle. Hankinta sisältää yhteensä neljän (4) lääkärin ostopalvelun Hatanpään sosiaali- ja terveysaseman ja Tammelakeskuksen sosiaali- ja terveysaseman alueiden omapotilaiden hoidon toteuttamiseksi. Ammatinharjoittajamallilla tuotetaan yleislääkäripalvelut kokonaisvaltaisesti hoidon jatkuvuusmallin kriteerien mukaisille omapotilaille, jotka asuvat yrittäjälääkärille osoitetun sote-aseman alueella. Yrittäjälääkäri toimii omalääkärinä, joka on hoitovastuussa omapotilaistaan. Omalääkärin työparina toimii omahoitaja. Yrittäjälääkäri toimii yhteistyössä tilaajan henkilöstön kanssa osana sote-aseman moniammatillista toimintaympäristöä. Palvelussa keskeistä ovat hoidon saatavuuden sekä hoidon jatkuvuuden parantaminen. Palvelu tuotetaan joko edellä mainituilla Tilaajan sosiaali- ja terveysasemilla tai Palveluntuottajan järjestämissä toimitiloissa. Toimitiloja koskevat sijaintivaatimukset on määritetty hankintasopimuksen liitteessä 2 Palvelukuvaus. Sopimuskausi alkaa 1.2.2027 ja on voimassa toistaiseksi. Hankinnan ennakoitu arvonlisäveroton vuosiarvo sitoumuksetta on noin 875 000 euroa. Palveluntuottajien valinta on kuvattu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnön kohdassa ”Päätöksenteon perusteet”. description: Gegenstand der Maßnahme ist der Schadstoffsanierung, Entkernung und Abbruch im Bereich des Verkehrsknotenpunktes (VKN) Hbf München. Für die Herstellung der Vorhaltemaßnahme U9 und des Neubau Empfangsgebäudes sollen die daran angrenzenden Bereiche (Durchgangshalle sowie Nord- und Südbau) abgebrochen werden. Die Abbruchmaßnahmen umfassen die oberirdischen Teile der beschriebenen Gebäudeteile wie auch die bestehenden Untergeschosse und somit die kompletten Bauwerke, inkl. aller Medien / Versorgungsanlagen. title: Finland – Gravel, sand, crushed stone and aggregates – Kivi- ja maa-aineksen puitesopimus
description: Puolustusvoimien logistiikkalaitos (jäljempänä Hankintayksikkö) pyytää tarjoustanne Kivi- ja maa-aineksen toimituksista Uudenmaan prikaatin ja Panssariprikaatin tarpeisiin, tämän tarjouspyynnön ja sen liitteiden mukaisesti. Kummankin joukko-osaston tarpeeseen valitaan yksi tai kaksi toimittajaa ja valittujen toimittajien kanssa tehdään puitesopimus joukko-osaston (jäljempänä tilaaja) käyttöön. Tarjouspyynnön kivi- ja maa-ainesten määrät ovat arvioituja yhteenlaskettuja määriä koko sopimuskaudelle, sopimuksen allekirjoittamisesta neljän (4) vuoden ajaksi ja ne voivat sopimuksen aikana ylittyä tai alittua arvioidusta. Tilattavan aineksen todellista määrää ei pystytä kertomaan tarkemmin, koska alueiden kunnostustyöt riippuvat siihen myönnetyistä määrärahoista ja alueiden käytöstä. Tilaajan yhteyshenkilöt tilaavat tarpeen ilmaantuessa erillisten tilausten perusteella sopimuksen mukaisia tuotteita valituilta toimittajilta.

title: Tampa Harbor Improvements Industry Day
description: This announcement constitutes a Special Notice. This announcement seeks information from industry and will only be used for preliminary planning purposes. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS AND NO CONTRACT SHALL BE AWARDED FROM THIS SPECIAL NOTICE. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation. This is a SAVE-THE-DATE special notice for an industry day event on 18 November 2026 at 9:00AM EST. All interested Offerors are required to access SAM.gov for future updates. Please view registration information and details below. The presentation slides and list of attendees will be made available and posted to the subject special notice on SAM.gov after the conclusion of the event. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Jacksonville District will be holding an Industry Day event to gauge the interest, capabilities, and qualifications of various members of the Construction Community, to include Small Businesses, and to also provide information and obtain feedback from interested Offerors prior to issuance of the official solicitation. This requirement is for fiscal year (FY) 2028 award. NAICS Code 237990: Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction Small Business Standard: $37 million Magnitude of Construction: $100 - $500 million Project Title: Tampa Harbor Improvements Industry Day. Purpose: The purpose of this scheduled Industry Day is to provide the latest information regarding the future advertisement and award of Contract 1 for the Tampa Harbor Deepening Project. The scheduled event will include a detailed presentation by the Jacksonville District US Army Corps of Engineers, Tampa Harbor Project Delivery Team (PDT) followed by open Q&A and 1-1 meeting opportunities with contracts to ask more in-depth questions and get feedback as the design and permitting moves forward. Project Description: The project includes construction dredging to deepen and widen specified areas within the federal navigation channel of Tampa Harbor. The project is planned for six (6) contracts over an estimated 8�10-year period. The Scope of Work for this Industry Day will be focused on Contract 1. Contract 1 work includes deepening of Cut-C (HB), Port Sutton Channel, Port Sutton Turning Basin, East Bay Channel and Cut-D (HB) to a depth of 49 feet MLLW, deepening the Port Sutton Terminal Channel to a depth of 44 feet MLLW, and deepening the East Bay Channel Extensions 1 and 2 to a depth of 41 feet MLLW. The Contract 1 work also includes widening of Port Sutton Channel, Port Sutton Turning Basin, and East Bay Channel. All areas of deepening and widening will incorporate +1 foot of allowable overdepth. All dredged material from the project will be disposed of in the East Bay Placement Area, DMMA 2-D and DMMA 3-D. Estimated quantities to be dredged are roughly 4.4 million cubic yards. description: N00164-27-S-NC12 - REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI)/SOURCES SOUGHT � ENVIRONMENTAL QUALIFICATION TESTING (EQT) - PSC H270 - NAICS 541380 Issue Date: 29 OCT 2026 - Closing Date: 18 NOV 2026 - 11:00 AM EST REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) - The Government is issuing this RFI/sources sought announcement as part of market research for usage of Environmental Qualification Testing (EQT). The objective is to engage a qualified testing contractor to perform environmental qualification testing (EQT) to verify that this updated enclosure assembly and workstation mount meets all naval shipboard survival and operational requirements. The Statement of Work (SOW) defines the requirements for environmental and electromagnetic compatibility testing of the Combined All-Domain Command and Control System Afloat (CAC2S Afloat) Data Processing Assembly and Workstation Mount. See attached SOW to review the technical requirements provided as Attachment 1 to this document. Vendors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) and registered in the Joint Certification Program (JCP) in order to receive access to the SOW. Information about the JCP is located at https://www.public.dacs.dla.mil/. In accordance with Department of Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Procedures, Guidance, and Information (PGI) 206.302-1, the Government is accepting information from companies potentially capable of meeting the requirements as described above. Companies with the capabilities and facilities to provide this testing that meets the Government�s requirements and certification requirements may respond. Responses shall address requirements as discussed within the SOW. All interested parties may submit company and product literature, a white paper no longer than 5 pages, and/or other pertinent information, such as a description with performance parameters and a statement of current availability, summary of prior testing, test reports, a budgetary estimate, and an explanation as to why the Government should not procure this effort on a sole source basis as stated above given the requirements set forth. Responses to the Market Survey shall include the following: Submitter�s Name Street Address, City, State, Zip Code Business Size Point of Contact (POC) POC Telephone Announcement Number: N00164-27-S-NC12 Please include the purpose/explanation of the response to the Market Survey, i.e. to better understand the Government requirements; to potentially become a viable source for future requirements; to take exception to the anticipated sole source as your company currently meets all of the Government requirements. The Government may contact RFI respondents to get clarification on the information submitted. Submissions may be sent by any government or non- governmental entity including commercial firms, non-profit organizations, and institutions of higher education with degree-granting programs in science and/or engineering (universities), or by consortia comprising such concerns. Responses from Small and Small Disadvantaged Business firms are highly encouraged. Firms responding should indicate if they are a small business, a socially and economically disadvantaged business, 8(a) firms, historically black colleges or universities, and minority institutions. Contractors must be properly registered in the Government's System for Award Management (SAM) and in the Joint Certification Program (JCP) in order to receive the attachments. Offerors may obtain information on SAM registration and annual confirmation requirements by calling 1-866-606-8220 or via the Internet at https://www.sam.gov. Information about on JCP is located at https://www.public.dacs.dla.mil/. At the current time, NO FUNDING IS AVAILABLE for contractual efforts. This RFI/sources sought does not constitute an Invitation for Bids (IFB), a Request for Quote (RFQ), or a Request for Proposal (RFP) and it should not be construed as a commitment of any kind by the government to issue a formal solicitation or ultimately award a contract. The US Government is in no way liable to pay for or reimburse any companies or entities that respond to this announcement. Any costs incurred by interested companies in response to this announcement will NOT be reimbursed. Market Survey information may be submitted to the Point of Contact (POC) any time prior to the expiration of this announcement. The POC for this effort is Ms. Morgan Helton, morgan.m.helton.civ@us.navy.mil Responses to this RFI/sources sought may be emailed to the POC above. If any part of the submittal is classified, please contact the POC for appropriate submission information. All information marked as proprietary information will be safeguarded to prevent disclosures to non-government personnel and entities.

Office of Hazardous Materials Safety Research Initiative � FY2026 BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA)
description: AMENDMENT 02 (09/21/2026): The purpose of this amendment is to incorporate PHMSA�s Responses to Vendor Inquiries regarding Phase I white paper submissions, subcontractor eligibility for foreign entities, submission limits, deadlines, and multi-topic proposals under the solicitation (See attached). All other terms and conditions of the solicitation remain unchanged. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- AMENDMENT 01 (08/24/2026): The purpose of this amendment is to (1) change the Phase I White Paper due date from December 22, 2026, to November 18, 2026, and (2) add the contact email address tremayne.terry@dot.gov to Section X.A. in Attachment 1- BAA Solicitation_PHMSA-26HM-BAA. All other terms and conditions of the solicitation remain unchanged. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT), Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA), Office of Hazardous Materials Safety (OHMS), is soliciting white papers and full proposals under Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) PHMSA-26HM-BAA pursuant to FAR 35.016. The objective of this announcement is to award competitive research contracts that advance scientific, technical, engineering, and policy solutions to prevent incidents and enhance safety during the transportation of hazardous materials across all modes. Offerors are invited to submit innovative research proposals addressing one or more of the following core topic areas: 26HM-ESS (Efficient Safety Standards): Research to modernize safety standards and testing, streamline certification, leverage safety data, and evaluate risk landscapes to reduce regulatory burden while maintaining safety. 26HM-SST (Safe Energy Storage Technologies): Research assessing transportation risks of energy storage systems, battery chemistries, thermal runaway detection and mitigation, and critical mineral recovery. 26HM-IPG (Innovative Packaging): Development and evaluation of advanced packaging materials, containment designs, integrity monitoring, and predictive failure simulations. 26HM-RER (Risk Reduction for Emergency Response): Innovations, technologies, data analysis, and materials to enhance emergency responder safety, communication, and preparedness. 26HM-RTS (Hazardous Materials Rail Transportation Safety): Research advancing scientific understanding of rail tank car performance under derailment conditions, crashworthiness materials, thermal shielding, and predictive risk modeling. A two-phase selection process (Phase I: White Paper; Phase II: Invited Full Proposal) will be used. Awards will be procurement contracts (Firm-Fixed-Price or Cost-Reimbursement) up to $2,000,000 with a total performance period of up to 36 months. Full eligibility, formatting, and submission instructions are detailed in the solicitation document attached to this notice.

title: Personal Radiation Detector (PRD)
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) SUMMARY: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), Office of Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) requires Personal Radiation Detectors (PRDs). PRDs are pager-size devices worn by users for radiological and nuclear detection capability as well as personal protection. PRDs automatically monitor the environment and alert the user when radiation levels above the natural background are detected. PRDs also assist the user in localizing the source of detected radiation. The high sensitivity and rapid response time to the variations in the ambient radiation levels clearly distinguish PRDs from the family of electronic dosimeters which are mainly used for accurate dose and dose rate. GENERAL INFORMATION: This RFI is issued solely for information gathering purposes to identify offerors that can provide identify commercially available, gamma-detecting Personal Radiation Detectors (PRDs), including available wireless-communication and data-transmission capabilities in advance of an acquisition which will include testing of the most compliant candidate solutions. In accordance with FAR 15.201(e), RFIs may be used when the Government wants to obtain price, delivery, other market information, and capabilities for planning purposes. Responses to these RFIs are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. This RFI shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government for any purpose, nor does it restrict the Government to an ultimate acquisition approach. Respondents are solely responsible for all expenses associated with their RFI response. Respondents will not receive additional information in response to their submittal to the RFI and will not be notified of the resulting market research. Interested parties must submit sufficient documentation in accordance with the instructions in this RFI and current industry�s best practices and standards, demonstrating their ability/experience to meet or exceed the Government�s requirements listed in this notice. RFI RESPONSE SUBMITTAL INSTRUCTIONS: Interested contractors shall submit their RFI responses electronically to Isaac Chapple, Contracting Officer, at Isaac.Chapple@fema.dhs.gov no later than 12:00PM Eastern Standard Time (EST), (due 11/18/2026).

title: Coburn Gore LPOE Art in Architecture Project
description: Document Added & Updated: 0332CG-AIA- Coburn Gore AIA Questions & Answers V3 Dated 07 October 2026 The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) Art in Architecture Program commissions American artists (citizens and Lawful Permanent Residents or Permanent Workers of the United States) to create publicly scaled and permanently installed artworks for Federal buildings nationwide. GSA announces an opportunity for a Federal art commission in conjunction with the new construction of the Coburn Gore Land Port of Entry (LPOE) in Coburn, Maine. The new facility will strengthen supply chains, improve operational capabilities and facility infrastructure, spur economic growth, and bolster the country�s security. The project will provide a fully operational LPOE that coordinates with the tra?c ?ow and operations of the Canadian port of entry at Saint-Augustin-de-Woburn Quebec, Port of Entry. The project will provide a new port that allows Customs and Border Protection to more efficiently carry out its agency mission, their operations and interactions with the public. GSA allocates one-half of one percent (0.5%) of the estimated construction costs of new or modernized Federal facilities for art commissions. The art budget for this project is estimated to be between $275,000 to $400,000. One or more artists will be awarded a fixed-price contract for a commission. Artists who wish to be considered for this GSA art commission must submit application materials to GSA by the SAM Contract Opportunity�s Response Date. Artists may also elect to be considered for all future GSA art commissions by submitting application materials to GSA�s National Artist Registry (Registry). Instructions on how to submit application materials and join the Registry are available on the following Web site: https://www.gsa.gov/real-estate/design-and-construction/art-in-architecturefine-arts/art-in-architecture-program/art-in-architecture-national-artist-registry All artists who wish to be considered as candidates for a commission at the LPOE in Coburn Gore, ME must have their application materials submitted and received by GSA by 12:00 PM Eastern Time on 18 November 2026. Artists� submissions received after the deadline will not be considered for this project but will be eligible for consideration on future GSA commissions alongside the other artists on the Registry. Artists already on the Registry need not resubmit but may elect to update their information prior to the deadline. GSA evaluates artists based on the following criteria: the media, materials, content and style of the artist�s past work, along with the artist�s past performance and experience with commissions or projects similar to the one described in this synopsis. Shortlisted artists will be contacted and asked to submit additional information, including a statement that the artist can perform the work associated with the GSA commission within the identified budget. GSA will count the combined weight of all the selection criteria as significantly more important than price. At minimum, the scope of services for this commission will require collaboration with the lead designer selected for the land port of entry project; travel to the project site; development and presentation of preliminary and final concepts; fabrication of the artwork; participation in meetings and conservation reviews as necessary; delivery and installation of the artwork; professional documentation of, and detailed maintenance planning for the artwork at the project site. For informational purposes: Artists selected for the contract award must be Permanent Residents or Citizens of the United States of America. Artists selected for the contract award will be required to have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) at the time of award. Instructions for creating an account and activating registration in SAM may be found at www.sam.gov. Artists selected for the contract award will be required to renew the registration in SAM on an annual basis for the duration of the project. In accordance with Executive Order (EO) 13934, agencies should prioritize the commission of works of art that portray historically significant Americans or events of American historical significance or illustrate the ideals upon which our Nation was founded. Inquiries concerning the project should be directed to the following email address: Molly.Lewis@gsa.gov and reference the synopsis number in the subject line. No questions will be answered after 07 October 2026 12:00pm EST.

title: End of the World Long Term Stewardship
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Proposals are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 12363N26R4016 is issued as a Request for Proposal (RFP) for the End of the World G-Z Long-Term IRSC (EOTW G-Z LTIRSC). The End of the World Project area is approximately 50,000 acres on the Salmon River Ranger District of the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forest. The End of the World EIS authorizes commercial treatment on over 17,000 acres primarily through intermediate harvest. The purpose of the EOTW G-Z LTIRSC is to thin overstocked stands to reduce the risk of catastrophic wildfire as well as improve stand health. The EOTW Project is within the Wildland Urban Interface and has numerous private inholdings with seasonal and permanent residents. This contracting tool will increase the pace and scale of active management beyond the current capacity of staffing levels. A secondary objective of the EOTW G-Z LTIRSC is to provide a steady, dependable supply of timber and forest products to local facilities. This project aligns with Secretarial Memo 1078-006 and the Implementation of Secretarial Memo 1078-006 dated April 3, 2025 to utilize long term stewardship contracts for active management. This acquisition is not set-aside for small business concerns. The applicable North American Industry Classification Standard Code is 113310 and the small business size standard is 500 Employees This acquisition is an unrestricted requirement. All responsible sources may submit a proposal and offer which will be considered by the agency. Proposals are to be submitted via email to Mark Phillipp at mark.phillipp@usda.gov and Matt Daigle at matthew.daigle@usda.gov.

title: NGA HRM-II RFP
description: The National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA) is to issue this Request for Proposal (RFP) HM047626R0018 for public response for the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA) Human Resource Management II (HRM II). The HRM II RFP will be a commercial effort under FAR Part 12, and the Government anticipates using Best Value � Tradeoff evaluation methods and acquisition procedures as described in FAR Part 15. Contract award will be made to the offeror who provides the best overall value to the Government in terms of evaluation factors listed in Section 5 of the RFP. The procurement will be conducted using full and open competition procedures. The Government contemplates award of a performance-based contract using Firm Fixed Price (FFP) and Time-and-Materials (T&M) CLINs resulting from the solicitation. The period performance is anticipated to be a one (1) year base period with four (4) twelve (12) month option periods. The HRM II acquisition includes: The National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency requires comprehensive Human Resource Management support services across the employee lifecycle. The requirement includes support for functions such as personnel data processing, talent acquisition support, talent development support, strategic workforce planning, employee support services, performance records management, benefits processing, retirement tracking, and related HR management support activities. In order to be considered for this requirement, the offeror shall have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM), https://www.sam.gov. Offerors may obtain information on SAM registration and annual confirmation requirements by calling 1-866-606-8220 or via the internet at https://www.sam.gov. title: Automated Ultrasound-Based, Super Intelligence (SI)-Enabled Fracture Detection
description: The Center for Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority (BARDA) intends to use responses to this Sources Sought Notice (SSN) for planning purposes. BARDA will not award any contracts under this Notice, but rather seeks current and forecasted prices, inventories, capabilities, and other pertinent marketplace data. This Notice is issued by the Center for Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority (BARDA) to identify innovative medical countermeasure technologies to enable rapid triage of musculoskeletal injuries such as fractures and soft tissue injuries of extremities. This request is for information only and is intended to assess the current state of commercially available technologies and technologies nearing commercial availability that support automated ultrasound-based fracture detection using technologies commonly known as Artificial Intelligence (AI). Consistent with Executive Order 14434, �Inaugurating the Era of Super Intelligence,� AI- technologies are now referred to as Super Intelligence (SI) throughout this notice, including in the title and should be referred the same in the response. The Center for Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority (BARDA) intends to use responses to this Sources Sought Notice (SSN) to inform planning for the potential acquisition of ultrasound-based devices capable of capturing and displaying anatomical data. Potential acquisition and inventory approaches include device purchases or leases supported by vendor-managed inventory (VMI) arrangements. BARDA seeks information on technologies that could assist clinical care providers in visualizing or detecting musculoskeletal injuries, including fractures and soft tissue injuries, to support triage and initial treatment in emergency departments, urgent care centers, and field settings. These devices could also support continued evaluation and treatment in definitive orthopedic care settings, consistent with applicable regulatory authorizations and intended uses. The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) leads Federal public health and medical preparedness and response efforts, including supporting the research, development, acquisition, and availability of medical countermeasures (MCMs). These efforts address the health consequences of chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear (CBRN) threats, pandemic influenza, and emerging infectious diseases, including threats arising from deliberate, accidental, or naturally occurring events. This SSN supports planning for medical capabilities that could strengthen the Nation�s preparedness for and response to emergencies involving traumatic injuries. The Project BioShield Act of 2004 (Pub. L. No. 108-276) established authorities for procuring qualifying security countermeasures for the Strategic National Stockpile (SNS). The Pandemic and All-Hazards Preparedness Act of 2006 (Pub. L. No. 109-417) further strengthened the Nation�s medical countermeasure development and preparedness framework. The National Health Security Strategy 2023�2026 provides additional strategic context for strengthening preparedness, response, and recovery capabilities. Consistent with these preparedness objectives, this Sources Sought Notice seeks information on potential approaches to improve the availability and accessibility of relevant medical devices across health care settings. Approaches of interest include purchase, lease, vendor-managed inventory (VMI), and arrangements that combine access to devices with maintenance and readiness support. Information received will inform acquisition planning and assessment of these approaches, subject to applicable statutory authorities, acquisition requirements, and availability of funds. These documents represent the foundation for addressing the Nation�s CBRN MCM needs. Amongst the foundational documents referenced above, musculoskeletal injuries such as fractures resulting from nuclear blast explosions and structural collapse, as well as and other mass casualty events present significant challenges in both field and clinical settings which require prompt diagnosis for adjudication and triage of patients. Current standards of care rely heavily on radiography and CT imaging, which are often unavailable, delayed, or resource-constrained in austere environments, disaster response settings, or during patient surge conditions. Delayed or missed fracture diagnosis can worsen patient outcomes and burden downstream care. BARDA is seeking solutions that enhance the speed, accuracy, and accessibility of fracture detection at the point of injury and point of care, without dependence on traditional imaging infrastructure. CAPABILITY STATEMENT/INFORMATION SOUGHT This Sources Sought Notice (SSN) seeks information from small business (SB) and other than small business (OTSB) concerns regarding their qualifications, experience, and capabilities to develop, manufacture, and deploy standalone, point-of-care, super intelligence (SI)-enabled ultrasound devices for fracture detection. Respondents shall provide only the information, data, and materials necessary to demonstrate their capabilities relevant to this notice. Responses shall include separate Technical Representation and Business Representation sections, as detailed below. Each section shall not exceed 10 single-sided pages, including all attachments, r�sum�s, charts, and other supporting materials, and shall use 12-point Times New Roman font. Pages exceeding the limit for either section will not be reviewed. Respondents shall identify their business size status as either small business or other than small business under the NAICS code and corresponding size standard identified in this notice. Technical Representations Respondents shall provide the technical information requested by ASPR/BARDA in separately numbered sections, in the order listed below. For any section that does not apply, respondents shall retain the section number and heading, mark it �Not Applicable,� and briefly explain why it does not apply. Response Specification In response to this notice, clearly describe the capability and experience that meets the criteria specified in the subsequent categories. A template is provided for detailed and concise responses as related to the qualifying criteria. Additional supporting evidence, data, and information can be provided as attachments, not to exceed the 10-page limit per submission to this notice. All sponsors responding to this notice are required to provide the requested information on their products and capabilities by providing short responses, summarizing their device's diagnostic capability along with performance data, TRL and development status, regulatory documentation, product IFU, manufacturing overview, and supply-chain and production information. The narrative response to the templated prompts may include figures, schematics, diagrams, photographs, etc. and shall describe the proposed final product under consideration. Any proposed device must qualify against the following criteria (either work completed or demonstratable work in progress): Display and Diagnostic of Anatomy for Fracture Evaluation Capability Automated ultrasound imaging-based volumetric capture and display of detailed anatomy of different structures and providing bone detection/identification in areas such as wrist, ankles and others; and assist care providers to visualize clinically significant injuries such as fractures. Embedded ultrasound image processing information with appropriately trained Super Intelligence and machine learning (SI/ML) models to assist in image acquisition and segmentation for data interpretation with predefined sensitivity/specificity performance, which has been reviewed and adjudicated in FDA submissions for 510k clearance process. title: Request for Information for U-2 Advanced Synthetic Aperture Radar System -2
description: Amendment 1- Response due date was updated to Nov 18, 2026 03:00 pm EST. The RFI attachment has been updated. The Government is conducting market research to identify potential sources that possess the repair data, expertise, capabilities, manufacturing, engineering, software development, maintenance and experience to meet qualification requirements to repair and sustain the Advanced Synthetic Aperture Radar System (ASARS)-2 components and ground support equipment. The level of security clearance and amount of overseas continental United States participation in this requirement has not been determined. The Government does not own or have access to the data for the ASARS-2 sensor. The Government has determined that this system is a noncommercial item. The Air Force requires long-term support and sustainment of the ASARS-2, which provides near-real-time high-resolution, long-range imagery from ground returns during day or night, in all weather conditions. Air Combat Command A5 requirements provide for an over-arching sustainment program for the U-2. The Contract Logistics Support (CLS) includes engineering support, the repair of spare assets, resolution of system failures and issues to ensure availability, reliability, and maintainability of the fielded equipment and software. This effort requires cybersecurity support and sustainment in accordance with National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) SP 800-171, NIST SP 800-53, Intelligence Community Directive (ICD) 503, and the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) process, Cybersecurity Impact Evaluation Recommendation (CIER) for all changes and modifications of this effort to incorporate in the U-2S Approval to The Air Force requires long-term support and sustainment of the ASARS-2, which provides near-real-time high-resolution, long-range imagery from ground returns during day or night, in all weather conditions. Air Combat Command A5 requirements provide for an over-arching sustainment program for the U-2. The Contract Logistics Support (CLS) includes engineering support, the repair of spare assets, resolution of system failures and issues to ensure availability, reliability, and maintainability of the fielded equipment and software. This effort requires cybersecurity support and sustainment in accordance with National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) SP 800-171, NIST SP 800-53, Intelligence Community Directive (ICD) 503, and the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) process, Cybersecurity Impact Evaluation Recommendation (CIER) for all changes and modifications of this effort to incorporate in the U-2S Approval toOperate (ATO) package, Cybersecurity Authorization Package (CAP), Risk Management Framework (RMF), Interim Authority to Test (IATT), Interim Authority to Connect (ATC), and/or separate ATO, as applicable and requested by the Government. This effort also requires Depot Maintenance Support Teams (DMST) to support the following sustainment activities: mission software updates; Diminishing Manufacturing Sources (DMS) engineering; engineering change proposals; configuration management (hardware and software); integration with ASARS-related systems on the U-2 platform; data management; technical data (such as technical manuals and reports) development and maintenance; in-plant Specialized Repair Activity and sparing; technical and engineering actions for calibrating ASARS-2; resolving system failures/issues in a timely manner; and planning/preparation/implementation of system sustainment improvements.

description: The U.S. Army Contracting Command - New Jersey, on behalf of the office of the Project Manager, Combat Ammunition Systems (PM CAS), intends to issue a Request for Proposal (RFP) for Primer Feed Mechanisms (PFMs) in support of the M777A2 155mm Howitzer. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concern

description: US ARMY CORPS OF ENGINEERS (USACE) � LATIN AMERICA AND CARIBBEAN DISTRICT INDUSTRY DAY ANNOUNCEMENT: DAY 2 � CONSTRUCTION Requirement: Callao Naval Base, Peru, Infrastructure Modernization - Construction Customer Agency: Peruvian Navy Notice ID: W51DQV27Z1CV9 NAICS Code: 236220 � Commercial and Institutional Building Construction Associated Sources Sought: W51DQV27S1CQ0 Event Date: Wednesday, December 2, 2026 Location: Centro Naval Sede San Borja, Lima, Peru RSVP Deadline: November 18, 2026, at 3:00 pm CT General Overview The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Caribbean District, is hosting an Industry Day event in Lima, Peru, to engage with industry partners regarding the upcoming acquisition of the Callao Naval Base, Peru, Infrastructure Modernization Project and NAMRU-S O&M Project. To provide focused engagement for distinct industry sectors, the event is structured over three specialized days: Day 1 (Tuesday, December 1, 2026): Callao Naval Base, Peru, Infrastructure Modernization Project - Architecture & Engineering (A/E) Services (NAICS 541330) Day 2 (Wednesday, December 2, 2026): Callao Naval Base, Peru, Infrastructure Modernization Project - Construction (NAICS 236220) Day 3 (Thursday, December 3, 2026): U.S. Navy Medical Research Unit South (NAMRU-S) Lima and Iquitos, Peru - Facilities Operation and Maintenance (O&M) Services (NAICS 561210) This announcement specifically covers Day 2 (Construction). Separate announcements address Day 1 (A/E Services) and Day 3 Facilities Operation and Maintenance (O&M). Purpose of the Event The purpose is to present the planned Design-Build construction requirements for the shoreside modernization at Callao, brief prospective prime contractors and subcontractors on USACE contracting and technical standards, explain federal registration procedures, and conduct one-on-one market research capability briefings. Summary of the Sessions The program includes three distinct sessions: Construction: A comprehensive briefing on project scope, facility packages, technical specifications, procurement timelines, and USACE compliance requirements. One-on-One Capability Briefings: Private, scheduled 15-minute briefings reserved for prospective Prime Contractors to present capabilities directly to the USACE acquisition team. Federal Systems Registration Support: Individual, walk-in technical assistance to help prospective contractors navigate SAM.gov, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), and NCAGE. Please note: This announcement is issued solely for market research and informational planning purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP), an Invitation for Bids (IFB), or an obligation on the part of the U.S. Government. No contract award will result directly from this event. Logistics & Schedule Date: December 2, 2026 Hours: 08:30 � 4:00 PM AT/Local Lima Time Location: Centro Naval Sede San Borja Av. San Luis S/N� Cdra. 24, Urb. San Borja Sur, Lima, Peru Daily Schedule Note: A detailed schedule of presentations, networking intervals, and allocated session times is currently being finalized. The specific daily agenda will be published in a forthcoming update to this announcement prior to the event. Event Details & Specific Sessions Session 1: Construction Seminar & Project Scope Briefing USACE project and contracting representatives will deliver a detailed technical presentation covering: Detailed project background and site layout for the Callao Naval Base. Design-Build technical parameters, civil and structural works, industrial warehousing, and specialized mechanical/electrical/plumbing (MEP) systems. Acquisition milestones, contract structure, evaluation criteria, and Defense Base Act (DBA) insurance requirements. Practical guidance on doing business with USACE and U.S. Federal Government contracting standards. Session 2: One-on-One Capability Briefings (Pre-Registration Required) Prospective Prime Contractors (including formal Joint Ventures and Prime Mentor-Prot�g� partnerships) may request a dedicated 15-minute private session with the USACE acquisition panel. Objective: Market research to assess industry interest, bonding capacity, construction methodologies, and regional execution capabilities. Eligibility: Strictly reserved for entities intending to submit a proposal as a Prime Contractor. Availability: Time slots are limited and will be confirmed on a strictly first-come, first-served basis upon receipt and validation of the RSVP form. Session 3: Federal Systems Registration Support Throughout the day, USACE specialists will host an individual support station to assist contractors with: Companies interested in receiving support should bring a computer. Navigating NATO Commercial and Government Entity (NCAGE) code applications. Obtaining a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and activating an account in SAM.gov. Project & Requirement Overview Project Description The contemplated acquisition will be executed as a complete Design-Build (D-B) contract. The scope of work encompasses: Post-award architectural and engineering final design. Geotechnical verification, bulk earthwork, site preparation, and foundation stabilization. Civil infrastructure, perimeter security, access roadways, and heavy-duty utility integration. Structural construction of industrial logistics, storage, and administrative facilities. Advanced mechanical, electrical, plumbing (MEP), climate-control, fire suppression, and cold-chain systems. Complete Furniture, Fixtures, & Equipment (FF&E) packages. Statutory Defense Base Act (DBA) insurance coverage and host-nation environmental/building compliance. Summary of Facility Packages Building 110 Primary Function: Spare Parts Warehouse Key Technical Considerations: Heavy-duty slab design, industrial racking integration, material handling flow, automated logistics staging. Building 115 Primary Function: Clothing & Gear Warehouse Key Technical Considerations: High-density pallet storage, humidity and climate control, inventory distribution bays. Building 112 Primary Function: Material Warehouse Key Technical Considerations: Bulk staging, overhead crane/hoist accommodations, heavy equipment ingress/egress ramps. Building 113 Primary Function: Customs Warehouse Key Technical Considerations: Secure bonded holding areas, host-nation customs inspection layout, physical security infrastructure. Building 114 Primary Function: Petroleum, Oil, and Lubricants (POL) Warehouse Key Technical Considerations: Secondary containment, explosion-proof electrical systems, specialized foam/water fire suppression, environmental drainage controls. Building 111 Primary Function: Medicine & Medical Supplies Warehouse Key Technical Considerations: Temperature/humidity-controlled storage (cold chain capability), pharmaceutical-grade clean finishings, backup power integration. Building 120 Primary Function: DIRNOTEMAT & Quality Control Building Key Technical Considerations: Administrative offices, testing and quality inspection laboratories, specialized testing benches, IT/telecom infrastructure. Site & Ancillary Works Primary Function: Infrastructure & Integration Key Technical Considerations: Site grading, structural fill, perimeter security, access roads, utility connections, complete FF&E packages, and host-nation compliant permitting. Streamlined RSVP & Venue Access Instructions Due to facility capacity constraints and military installation security protocols at Centro Naval, advance registration is mandatory. Attendance is limited to a maximum of three (3) representatives per company. To simplify the registration process, interested firms must follow this two-step procedure: Step 1 � Email Request: Send an email to Claudia Montero at Claudia.M.Montero@usace.army.mil, and cc Renee Booth, Meranda.R.Booth@usace.army.mil, and Jaclyn Yocum, Jaclyn.C.Yocum@usace.army.mil , no later than November 18, 2026, at 3:00 pm CT. title: Tax Software and Support
description: The IRS has an ongoing requirement for commercial tax software products and associated services supporting the Federal Tax Compliance mission. The anticipated contract will provide software licenses, customization, software maintenance, integration, training, and user and technical support. The requirement includes, but is not limited to: Up to 130 Tax Analyzer licenses and annual renewals; Up to 150 Tax Planner licenses and annual renewals; Tax software user and technical support/help desk services; Maintenance of IRS-customized Issue Management System (IMS) Tax Engine Middleware; Support and maintenance of the Tax Engine Middleware Plug-In; Software customization and integration; Annual face-to-face training for up to 25 participants; Quarterly virtual training for licensed users; Software updates, upgrades, patches, and enhancements; Integration and testing support; and Associated program management, cybersecurity, documentation, and technical support services. Anticipated Period of Performance Base Period: December 18, 2026 - December 17, 2027 Option Period 1: December 18, 2027 - December 17, 2028 Option Period 2: December 18, 2028 - December 17, 2029 Option Period 3: December 18, 2029 - December 17, 2030 Option Period 4: December 18, 2030 - December 17, 2031 The government anticipates awarding a single firm-fixed-price contract utilizing a Best-Value Tradeoff (BVTO) source selection approach in accordance with FAR 15.101-1. Proposals will be evaluated based on the following factors, listed in descending order of importance: Technical Approach Licensing, Middleware Integration & Support Capability Past Performance Price The combined non-price factors are significantly more important than price. Award will be made to the responsible offeror whose proposal represents the best value to the government, considering price and non-price factors. The government intends to award without discussions; however, it reserves the right to conduct discussions if determined necessary by the Contracting Officer. Questions and Proposal Submission Questions Due: October 30, 2026, at 4:00 PM Eastern Time. Proposals Due: November 18, 2026, at 4:00 PM Eastern Time. All questions and proposals shall be submitted electronically via email to both: louis.c.browniii@irs.gov tanya.r.burnett@irs.gov Offerors shall submit proposals in accordance with Section L, Instructions, Conditions, and Notices to Offerors, and Section M, Evaluation Factors for Award, of the attached solicitation. Interested offerors are encouraged to carefully review the solicitation and all accompanying attachments for complete technical requirements, proposal instructions, evaluation criteria, and applicable terms and conditions. Any amendments, clarifications, or updates to this solicitation will be posted on SAM.gov. Offerors are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov for updates and amendments throughout the solicitation period.

title: Cross Over Network Waveguide Assembly Qualification and Production (P/Ns G638416-1)
description: The United States Government is conducting market research to identify potential sources that may possess the expertise, capabilities, and experience to meet the requirements for qualification and production of X-Band Cross Over Network. Security Requirements: The level of security clearance and amount of foreign participation in this requirement has not been determined; however, the Contractor should anticipate working with teams consisting of military, civilian, national partners, and contract personnel from various services and agencies. DISCLAIMER: THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP), REQUEST FOR QUOTE (RFQ) OR AN INVITATION FOR BID (IFB). IN ACCORDANCE WITH FAR 15.201(e), THIS NOTICE DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT.NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. THE GOVERNMENT MAY USE THE INFORMATION OBTAINED FROM RESPONSES TO THIS NOTICE IN DETERMINING ITS ACQUISITION APPROACH. THE ISSUANCE OF THIS NOTICE DOES NOT RESTRICT THE GOVERNMENT ACQUISTION APPROACH. The documents below contain a description of the Cross Over Network requirements, technical data package, and a Contractor Capability Survey. The Survey allows Contractors to provide their company's capability. Attention Small Business Respondents who are interested in participation for this effort: 1. No set aside decision has been made; however, the USG will determine the final strategy after thorough analysis of the small business responses and other market research available, considering the demonstrated interest and capability. Please ensure that you provide a thorough response to each question. If you company does not currently possess the full capability required to fulfill the entire requirment, what teaming/partnership/joint venture/subctonracting arrangements do you have in place to fulfill the Government's needs? Provide evidence of this arrangement e.g. emails, letter, etcl. that demonstrate a united response to this Sources Sought is highly encouraged, but not required. The evidence should state the type of arrangement and the role each member will fulfill. If you are only interested in being a subcontractor to the future awardee, state the portion of the work your organization has capability of fulfilling. 2. Identify any areas of work that your organization believes should be broken out exclusively for Small Businesses. Both Large and Small Businesses are encouraged to participate in this Market Research. Joint Ventures or Teaming Arrangements are encouraged. Questions relative to this market survey should be addressed to Brandon Jones, Contracting Officer, AFLCMC/ESGK-R (brandon.jones.96@us.af.mil) and Elizabeth Fuller (elizabeth.fuller.2@us.af.mil), Lead System Engineer, and Robert Cowden (robert.cowden.ctr@us.af.mil). Contract or Acquisition Specific questions shall be soley directed to the Contracting Officers. All questions shall be submitted in writing. Responses shall be received no later than the date identified in this posting.

title: Industry Day - Facilities Operation and Maintenance Services U.S. Navy Medical Research Unit South (NAMRU-S) Lima and Iquitos, Peru
description: US ARMY CORPS OF ENGINEERS (USACE) - LATIN AMERICA AND CARIBBEAN DISTRICT (SAA) INDUSTRY DAY ANNOUNCEMENT: DAY 3 OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE - SERVICES Requirement: Facilities Operation and Maintenance (O&M) - Services Customer Agency: U.S. Navy Medical Research Unit South (NAMRU-S) Lima and Iquitos, Peru Notice ID: W51DQV27Z1CV1 NAICS Code: 561210 - Facilities Support Services Associated Sources Sought: W51DQV27S1CQK Event Date: Wednesday, December 3, 2026 Location: Centro Naval Sede San Borja, Lima, Peru RSVP Deadline: November 18, 2026, at 3:00 pm (Local Lima Time) General Overview The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Caribbean District, is hosting an Industry Day event in Lima, Peru, to engage with industry partners regarding the upcoming acquisition of the Callao Naval Base, Peru, Infrastructure Modernization Project and NAMRU-S O&M Project. To provide focused engagement for distinct industry sectors, the event is structured over three specialized days: Day 1 (Tuesday, December 1, 2026): Callao Naval Base, Peru, Infrastructure Modernization Project - Architecture & Engineering (A/E) Services (NAICS 541330) Day 2 (Wednesday, December 2, 2026): Callao Naval Base, Peru, Infrastructure Modernization Project - Construction (NAICS 236220) Day 3 (Thursday, December 3, 2026): U.S. Navy Medical Research Unit South (NAMRU-S) Lima and Iquitos, Peru - Facilities Operation and Maintenance (O&M) Services (NAICS 561210). This announcement specifically covers Day 3 Facilities Operation and Maintenance (O&M). Separate announcements address Day 1 (A/E Services) and Day 2 (Construction). Purpose of the Event The purpose is to present the facilities operation and maintenance support requirements for the U.S. Navy Medical Research Unit South (NAMRU-S) facilities located in Lima and Iquitos, brief prospective prime contractors and subcontractors on USACE contracting and technical standards, explain federal registration procedures, and conduct one-on-one market research capability briefings. Summary of the Sessions The program includes three distinct sessions: Services Seminar: A comprehensive briefing on project scope, facility packages, technical specifications, procurement timelines, and USACE compliance requirements. One-on-One Capability Briefings: Private, scheduled 15-minute briefings reserved for prospective Prime Contractors to present capabilities directly to the USACE acquisition team. Federal Systems Registration Support: Individual, walk-in technical assistance to help prospective vendors navigate SAM.gov, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), NCAGE, and PIEE registration. Please note: This announcement is issued solely for market research and informational planning purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP), an Invitation for Bids (IFB), or an obligation on the part of the U.S. Government. No contract award will result directly from this event. Logistics & Schedule Date: December 3, 2026 Hours: 08:30 � 4:00 PM Local Lima Time Location: Centro Naval Sede San Borja Av. San Luis S/N� Cdra. 24, Urb. San Borja Sur, Lima, Peru Daily Schedule Note: A detailed schedule of presentations, networking intervals, and allocated session times is currently being finalized. The specific daily agenda will be published in a forthcoming update to this announcement prior to the event. Event Details & Specific Sessions Session 1: Services Seminar & Project Scope Briefing USACE project and contracting representatives will deliver a detailed technical presentation covering: Detailed laboratory recurring operations and maintenance, preventive maintenance , unscheduled maintenance, service-order support, minor repairs, specialty-system repairs, materials management, inventory control, technical reporting, quality control, and safety management. Acquisition milestones, contract structure, evaluation criteria, and Defense Base Act (DBA) insurance requirements. Practical guidance on doing business with USACE and U.S. Federal Government contracting standards. Session 2: One-on-One Capability Briefings (Pre-Registration Required) Prospective Prime Contractors (including formal Joint Ventures and Prime Mentor-Prot�g� partnerships) may request a dedicated 15-minute private session with the USACE acquisition panel. Objective: Market research to assess industry interest, service methodologies, and regional execution capabilities. Eligibility: Strictly reserved for entities intending to submit a proposal as a Prime Contractor. Availability: Time slots are limited and will be confirmed on a strictly first-come, first-served basis upon receipt and validation of the RSVP form. Session 3: Federal Systems Registration Support (SAM.gov & PIEE) Throughout the day, USACE specialists will host an individual support station to assist Peruvian and international contractors with: Navigating NATO Commercial and Government Entity (NCAGE) code applications. Obtaining a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and activating an account in SAM.gov. Firms interested in receiving support should bring a computer. Project & Requirement Overview The contemplated acquisition will be executed as a complete Services contract. The scope of work encompasses the facilities operation and maintenance services for NAMRU-S facilities located in Lima and Iquitos, Peru. Streamlined RSVP & Venue Access Instructions Due to facility capacity constraints and military installation security protocols at Centro Naval, advance registration is mandatory. Attendance is limited to a maximum of three (3) representatives per company. To simplify the registration process, interested firms must follow this two-step procedure: Step 1 � Email Request: Send an email to Claudia Montero at Claudia.M.Montero@usace.army.mil, and cc Renee Booth, Meranda.R.Booth@usace.army.mil and Angel J. Martinez, Angel.J.Martinez@usace.army.mil no later than November 18, 2026, at 3:00 pm (Local Lima Time). Subject Line: RSVP Request: NAMRU-S O&M Services Industry Day (Dec 3, 2026) � [Company Name] Message Body: State your company name, point of contact, contact email address, and interest in attending Day 3 (NAMRU-S O&M Services). Step 2 � Registration Form & Official Confirmation: Upon receipt of your email, Ms. Montero will reply with the official RSVP & Security Access Form. Complete the form (which collects attendee details, security credentials, and interest in 1-on-1 sessions or SAM.gov support) and return it via email. Upon review and clearance, Ms. Montero will issue an Official RSVP Confirmation Notice containing venue access instructions, check-in requirements, and confirmed one-on-one time slots (if requested). Event Documentation & Post-Event Postings To promote dynamic in-person dialogue and networking among prospective prime and subcontracting partners, detailed session slide decks, complete meeting agendas, and formal Q&A transcripts will not be published prior to the event. Pre-Event Distribution: Only logistical directions, security guidelines, and RSVP updates will be released prior to December 3, 2026. Post-Event Distribution: Following the conclusion of the event, the official presentation deck, the attendee directory (to facilitate joint ventures and teaming arrangements), and all formal Government answers to submitted questions will be posted publicly to SAM.gov under this Notice ID. Submission of Questions During the Event: Attendees may submit oral questions during designated Q&A periods or provide written questions on index cards distributed during registration. Post-Event Questions: Following the event, participants may submit technical and procurement inquiries via email to the points of contact listed below. All responses will be consolidated and posted publicly to SAM.gov. Federal Systems Registration (SAM.gov & PIEE) Prospective offerors are strongly encouraged to initiate federal vendor registrations immediately. There is no entitlement to payment by the Government of direct or indirect costs or charges that arise as a result of the submission of information in response to this request for information (RFI). The Government shall not be liable for or suffer any consequential damages for any improperly identified proprietary information. Proprietary information will be safeguarded in accordance with the applicable Government regulations. The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Savannah District is considering the solicitation and subsequent award of a Single Award Task Order Contract (SATOC) in support of the Formerly Used Defense Sites (FUDS) program. This requirement is for comprehensive support for the Formerly Used Defense Sites (FUDS) Program. The draft SOW defines the scope of program management, administrative, logistical, and community relations services necessary to execute and document FUDS projects. The range of activities includes maintaining and updating the FUDSMIS database, ensuring project documentation remains current, supporting Project Managers in developing and revising Project Management Plans and Site Management Action Plans, records management, preparation and coordination of key project documents, document uploads to the FUDS Documents portal, Cost-to-Complete estimate processes, logistics and community outreach support (including PDT and public meetings, Restoration Advisory Board activities, fact sheets, ROEs, and Section 508-compliant materials), and identification and implementation of efficiencies and streamlining measures. The Contractor shall undertake these support activities to achieve program objectives across FUDS projects and sites. Submission Instructions: Please follow the link below to access the survey.
